Alex K: Heads up — spot GPU interruption rate spiked in us-west over the last 48h. Thinking about reducing spot mix for Dedicated pools. Anyone have a quick FinOps read on realized savings vs the risk?
Maria R: Short version: raw price delta looks great but realized savings are lower once you account for restart overhead and tail latency.
Jordan L: Interruption rate in us-west jumped from ~3% to ~11% between 1718120000–1718200000. Median time-to-interrupt was ~6m, but tail interruptions caused some long retries.
Maria R: Numbers from last quarter: average spot price per GPU-hour $0.42, on-demand $1.12 => sticker savings ~62%. After restart/retry overhead and requeue delays, realized saving for our workloads was ~45%. Variance (stdev) of hourly price ~18%.
Sam F: Can you drop the quick formula you used? helps us model chargebacks.
Maria R: Sure — here's how we compute blended effective cost for a team:
```
blended_cost = (spot_hours * spot_effective_cost + ondemand_hours * ondemand_cost) / total_hours
spot_effective_cost = spot_price + (restart_hours * restart_penalty) / spot_hours
```
Example (simplified): spot_price=0.42, ondemand_cost=1.12, spot_hours=10k, restart_penalty equivalent=0.10 per spot-hour => blended ~0.60/GPU-hr (~46% vs on-demand).
Jordan L: Operational note: restart_penalty includes wasted compute on preempted work, scheduler latency, and higher egress from re-loading caches. For long-running inference containers the penalty is smaller than for training jobs.
Alex K: So teams running short jobs or stateless inference see better realized savings. If a team needs 99th p latency, spot might be problematic unless we pre-warm on-demand buffer.
Sam F: Proposal: move to mixed-capacity pools with policy: baseline 65% spot, 25% reserved on-demand buffer (pre-warmed), 10% burst overflow. Autoscaler switches weights when interruption >6% sustained.
Maria R: For chargeback: we recommend billing teams by 'consumed GPU-hours' at the blended effective rate computed monthly per pool. Also add an "interruption tax" allocation (small % reserve) to cover variance month-to-month rather than passing spikes immediately.
Alex K: Can we forecast the budget impact if we move from current 80% spot -> 65% spot mix?
Maria R: Quick calc: take current monthly GPU-hrs 200k. Current realized blended cost = $0.58/GPU-hr => $116k. New mix reduces expected interruptions, spot_effective_cost drops to $0.50 (because restart_penalty falls), ondemand hours up a bit. New blended ~0.66? wait let me run a quick on-paper:
```
current: 0.8*0.42 + 0.2*1.12 + restart_adj => ~0.58
new: 0.65*0.42 + 0.35*1.12 + smaller_restart_adj => ~0.72? hmm
```
Maria R: ok corrected numbers after spreadsheet: new blended = $0.68/GPU-hr (we traded some spot volume for guaranteed on-demand), monthly cost = 200k * 0.68 = $136k => +$20k/month. But risk exposure drops a lot (variance down ~40%).
Jordan L: So pay more for predictability. For customer-facing Dedicated SLAs this seems acceptable. For internal batch training teams maybe keep higher spot share and a separate chargeback policy.
Sam F: Action items: 1) eng-infra to implement mixed pool autoscaler policy (65/25/10) + pre-warm logic. 2) FinOps (Maria) to publish updated blended rates and chargeback calc. 3) SRE (Jordan) to add an interruption dashboard with per-region TTL and restart cost estimator.

Alex K: Thanks — let's sync after you post the updated rates. If anyone wants to A/B test 2-week pilot for a non-prod tenant, ping me. :thumbsup:
